bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial for modern tech: image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, autonomous vehicles.
Recent growth due to large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trains on labeled data to predict known outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Trains on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative rewards.
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust internal parameters.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for training the model and evaluating its performance.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, performing poorly on new data.
Underfitting: Model is too simple, failing to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationships for regression tasks.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicting class probabilities.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane for classification, effective in high-dimensional spaces.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the human brain, capable of learning complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Assess performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy, MSE.
Cross-Validation: Ensures model generalizes well by splitting data into multiple subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings for optimal performance using techniques like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: Complex models, especially deep learning, are difficult to understand.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting model generalization and performance.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased integration into daily life across healthcare, education, entertainment, and transportation.
Growing importance of ethical considerations and responsible AI practices as the field progresses.
